title: Client vs Server
summary: The fundamental split: one authoritative server runs the real game; each player's device runs a client that renders and inputs. They talk only through replication and remotes — and the server never trusts the client.

verification.notes: General client/server model page: create.roblox.com/docs/networking (client-server model).

explanation.whatItIs: Every Roblox game is two programs wearing one costume: the SERVER (one, authoritative, hidden) and the CLIENTS (one per player, renderers + input readers). Same code can run in both places but sees different worlds.
explanation.whyItExists: Multiplayer needs one source of truth. If clients decided damage or currency, cheaters would rule. The server decides; clients present.
whenToUse: Server: rules, state, saving, validation, economy, spawning
Client: input, camera, UI, sound, prediction and polish
whenNotToUse: Server for rendering concerns — it has no screen
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
        SERVER (truth)
   decides · validates · saves
        │            ▲
  replication     remotes
  (auto, down)  (explicit, both ways)
        ▼            │
CLIENT 1 … CLIENT n
  renders · reads input · predicts

Client says 'I want X'.
Server decides whether X happens.
```
tips: Ask 'who owns this?' for every system — ownership belongs to the server by default
LocalScripts = client, Scripts (default) = server, ModuleScripts = wherever required
Design latency-friendly: client acts instantly, server corrects if wrong
commonMistakes: Authoritative logic in LocalScripts (exploitable and unreliable)
Expecting client-created objects/state to exist on the server
Confusing Studio 'test' behavior (single-process) with production reality
Reading server-only services on the client and debugging nils

examples.title: Same module, both sides
examples.code:
-- SharedModule (ReplicatedStorage)
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local M = {}

function M.init()
    if RunService:IsServer() then
        print("Server: authoritative systems")
    else
        print("Client: UI and input systems")
    end
end

return M

-- Required from both a Script and a LocalScript,
-- each side takes its own branch.
